answer: An agent economy weights contract votes by escrowed stake. Agents named plume, juniper, and karst must each lock tokens for 30 days before voting. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight. To gain enough influence to control a vote, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more stake than honest voters, tying up capital and forgoing its use elsewhere throughout the lock period.
